ndss24.title: LiDAR Spoofing Meets the New-Gen: Capability Improvements, Broken Assumptions, and New Attack Strategies

icra25.title: SLAMSpoof: Practical LiDAR Spoofing Attacks on Localization Systems Guided by Scan Matching Vulnerability Analysis

ndss25.title: On the Realism of LiDAR Spoofing Attacks against Autonomous Driving Vehicle at High Speed and Long Distance

sets.title: Text injection: “IEEE S&P”
sets.note: Chosen Pattern Injection writes the letters “IEEE S&P” into free space in front of the sensor.

sets.title: Text injection: “Oakland”
sets.note: The same CPI spoofer drawing the word “Oakland” as a floating point pattern.

sets.title: 3D object injection: pedestrian and car
sets.note: Injected 3D pedestrian and vehicle point patterns, including a replayed copy of a real car captured by the same LiDAR. Recorded videos are matched to captures by timestamp.

sets.title: Dynamic injection: walking pedestrian
sets.note: A real walking person is captured, then replayed as a moving injected pedestrian. The capture of the real person is the benign reference.

sets.title: Pedestrian removal: PRA vs HFR
sets.note: A person walks in front of the LiDAR. The synchronized Physical Removal Attack (PRA) and the High-Frequency Removal (HFR) attack are compared with a benign run.

sets.title: Pedestrian removal in a corridor
sets.note: A person walks down a corridor towards the LiDAR, recorded benign, under a synchronized PRA, and under HFR.

sets.title: Vehicle removal in a parking lot
sets.note: HFR removes a parked car at about 5 m. No benign capture of this exact placement was found; the attack captures include periods with the spoofer off.

sets.title: Pedestrian removal in a parking lot
sets.note: HFR against a person walking between parked cars.

sets.title: Ghost-wall injection at 40 km/h
sets.note: The VLP-32C rides on a vehicle driving towards the roadside MVS system, which tracks the LiDAR and injects a ghost wall ahead of the vehicle. The camera clip starts two seconds before the capture.

sets.title: Ghost-wall injection at 30 km/h
sets.note: Same setup as the 40 km/h run, with the vehicle at 30 km/h.

sets.title: Injection runs on the test track
sets.note: Six consecutive injection runs against the vehicle-mounted VLP-32C. Run speeds were not recorded in the file names.

sets.title: Injection against a moving LiDAR on a cart
sets.note: An early outdoor test of the auto-aiming spoofer: the VLP-32C is pushed on a cart towards the MVS system.

sets.title: Indoor injection of a captured car
sets.note: A real car and a real pedestrian are first captured with the VLP-32C; the car trace is then injected as a spoofed vehicle. The captures of the real objects are the benign references.

sets.title: End-to-end attack on an Autoware vehicle
sets.note: PIXKIT with a VLP-32C, driven by Autoware.ai, benign vs. under attack (paper Fig. 16). Only the video is available; the LiDAR data of this run was not archived as pcap.

sets.title: A-HFR vs. HFR on AT128: pedestrian at 3 m
sets.note: AT128 has pulse fingerprinting. The plain HFR attack leaves most points in place (5 MHz) or is limited by laser overheating (15 MHz), while the adaptive HFR (A-HFR) at 15 MHz removes almost all points (paper Fig. 11).

sets.title: A-HFR attack width sweep on AT128
sets.note: A-HFR at 15 MHz with horizontal attack ranges from 10 to 60 degrees (paper Table VI).

sets.title: A-HFR attack width sweep on XT32
sets.note: A-HFR at 24 MHz with horizontal attack ranges from 10 to 60 degrees (paper Table VI). XT32 needs a higher frequency, so the removal rate drops faster as the range widens.

sets.title: A-HFR against AT128 on a moving vehicle
sets.note: The AT128 rides on a vehicle driving at 10–60 km/h past a pedestrian while the MVS system tracks it and fires A-HFR at 15 MHz (paper Table IX). Speeds and run numbers come from the file names; the benign drive is the reference used in the paper's analysis.

sets.title: Removal and injection seen by a VLP-16
sets.note: The two attack primitives SLAMSpoof places along a trajectory: HFR removal, which turns the attacked sector into scattered noise, and injection of a fake wall that the scan matcher latches onto.

sets.title: Attacking a moving WHILL from the roadside
sets.note: A WHILL CR2 carrying a VLP-32C drives across a sports field towards the tracking spoofer (under the tent), which attacks it from up to 50 m. The screen recording shows the localization output under attack. The LiDAR data of these runs is not on the lab drive, so this set is video only.

sets.title: Talk video: SMVS and spoofer placement
sets.note: The video shown in the ICRA 2025 talk: the Scan Matching Vulnerability Score, how it picks spoofer placements, and the attack results.
